title: Crochet Cords and Straps
description: Make ties, drawstrings, and shoulder straps that feel neat, sturdy, and comfortable to use.

content.summary: Cords and straps turn flat crochet pieces into useful bags, pouches, holders, and closures.
content.whyItMatters: A weak strap ruins an otherwise good project. A strong one makes handmade items feel dependable.
steps: Choose the right method for the job, such as chain-and-return cords, Romanian cord, or dense strap rows.
Keep your tension even so the cord does not twist or narrow in random spots.
Test the width and stretch before making a full-length strap.
Attach cords at strong points with extra stitches or secure seaming.
Check how the strap feels when the project has weight inside it.
content.practice: Make three short samples: a thin tie, a drawstring, and a wider shoulder strap.
commonMistakes: Using a strap that stretches too much for a heavy project.
Attaching the strap to a weak edge without reinforcement.
